user.account.external: This account comes from a directory and is managed there.
user.account.title: My Account
user.agents.empty: No agent is connected to your account.
user.agents.intro: Agents such as Claude that you connected through OAuth work with your rights. Disconnect one to cut it off at once.
user.agents.loadFailed: The connected agents could not be loaded
user.agents.revokeText: {name} loses its access at once and has to be connected again.

user.authorize.expired: This request has expired or was used already. Start the connection again from the agent.
user.authorize.heading: Connect {client} to Astrum Repository?
user.authorize.missing: This page opens when an agent asks to connect. Start the connection from the agent.
user.authorize.problemClient: The agent is not registered with this server. Start the connection again from the agent.
user.authorize.problemRedirect: The agent asked to return to an address it did not register, so the connection was stopped.
user.authorize.read: It can look around: search artifacts, read files and see the repositories, blob stores and tasks you can see.

user.form.emailRule: Enter an address such as jane@example.org
user.nugetKey.accessFailed: Could not get the NuGet API key. Check your credentials.
user.nugetKey.authAccess: Please authenticate to access your NuGet API key.
user.nugetKey.authReset: Please authenticate to reset your NuGet API key.
user.nugetKey.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
user.nugetKey.intro: Access your NuGet API key to authenticate NuGet package manager clients against this Astrum Repository instance.
user.nugetKey.keepSecret: Keep this key secret. Store it in your NuGet configuration, not in source code.
user.nugetKey.resetDone: API key reset. Generate a new one.
user.nugetKey.resetFailed: Could not reset the NuGet API key. Check your credentials.
user.nugetKey.resetText: This will permanently invalidate your current NuGet API key. Any NuGet clients using the existing key will fail to authenticate. You can generate a new key after resetting.
user.nugetKey.subtitle: Authentication key for NuGet package feeds
user.nugetKey.title: NuGet API Key
user.password.changed: Your password is changed. Your other sessions have ended.

user.password.intro.one: Choose a new password for your account. It needs at least {count} character.
user.password.intro.other: Choose a new password for your account. It needs at least {count} characters.

user.password.same: Choose a password other than the current one
user.password.title: Change Password
user.password.tooMany: Too many wrong passwords. Wait a few minutes and try again.
user.security.accessTokensNote: Access tokens and API keys do not need the second step.
user.security.codeHint: Enter the six-digit code the app shows now. If the code is refused, check that the clock of your device is correct.
user.security.codesOnce: These codes are shown only once
user.security.codesText: Each code signs you in once if you cannot use the app. Store them somewhere safe.
user.security.enrollBy: Set up an authenticator app by {date}.
user.security.enrollText: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the secret key by hand.
user.security.intro: Ask for a code from an authenticator app as a second step after your password.
user.security.managed: Two-factor authentication is managed by your identity provider.
user.security.passkeyAddText: Enter a name and your current password. Your browser then asks you to confirm the passkey with this device or a security key.
user.security.passkeyCancelled: The browser prompt was closed. No passkey was added.
user.security.passkeyFailed: The browser could not create the passkey.
user.security.passkeyNameHint: Up to 64 characters. Name the device or key, so you can tell your passkeys apart.
user.security.passkeyOtherRp: It was made for another address of this server, so it cannot be used here. Open the address it was made for to use it.
user.security.passkeyRenameText: Choose the name the list shows for this passkey.
user.security.passkeysIntro: Use a passkey from this device or a security key as a second step after your password.
user.security.passkeysOff: An administrator turned passkeys off on this server.
user.security.passkeysUnavailable: Passkeys are not available here: this server has no base URL to make them for. Ask an administrator to set one.
user.security.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
user.security.recoveryLow: Few recovery codes are left. Create new ones.
user.security.regenerateText: The current recovery codes stop working. Enter your password to create new ones.
user.security.removeText: Enter your password to remove the app.
user.security.removeWarning: Sign-in will then need only your password, unless your administrator requires a second factor.
user.security.required: Your administrator requires a second factor for this account.
user.security.restricted: Your session is limited until you set up an authenticator app.
user.security.setUpText: Enter your current password to start the set-up.
user.security.title: Security
user.tokens.empty: You do not have any access tokens yet.
user.tokens.emptyAll: Nobody has an access token yet.
user.tokens.intro: Use a token in place of your password in Docker, npm, Maven, pip and other clients. You can revoke it at any time and your password stays the same.
user.tokens.name: Name
user.tokens.namePlaceholder: such as Jenkins on the build host
user.tokens.noMatches: No access token matches your search.
user.tokens.once: Copy the token now. It is shown this one time only; if you lose it, create another one.
user.tokens.passwordFirst: You signed in with an access token. Tokens can only be created, listed and revoked after signing in with your password, so a leaked token cannot make more of itself.
user.tokens.passwordFirstTitle: Sign in with your password first
user.tokens.revokeText: Clients that use “{name}” stop working at once. This cannot be undone.
user.tokens.scopeWriteText: Everything you can do yourself, publishing included
user.tokens.title: Access Tokens
user.tokens.usageText: Sign in with your username as before and give the token instead of the password. Put the name of your repository in place of <repository>.
